title: Tissue Procurement: Cryopreservation with OCT Compound
author: Kerry Wiles
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6y7hfzn

steps.title: Prepare Tissue Samples
steps.instruction: Procure the requested anatomic site and tissue type, ensuring sizes are no larger than 0.4cm x 0.4cm x 0.3cm.

substeps.instruction: Cut tissue into approximately 1 cubic centimeter pieces.

steps.title: Prepare Cryomolds
steps.instruction: Arrange pre-labeled, UV sterilized clamshells on a block of dry ice to cool.

substeps.instruction: Ensure clamshells are laid evenly on the dry ice to allow for even OCT aliquoting.

steps.title: Prepare OCT Compound
steps.instruction: Invert the OCT compound to ensure no bubbles are introduced into the media and to avoid uneven distribution.

steps.title: Embed Tissue in OCT
steps.instruction: Fill each clamshell with an even layer of OCT, using a 30:1 OCT to tissue ratio, so that the OCT just touches all sides of the clamshell.

substeps.instruction: Using sterile forceps or a needle, transfer the specimen to the OCT-filled cryomold.
Gently submerge the tissue into the media in the correct orientation.
Cover the tissue with additional OCT until it is completely covered to ensure specimen integrity.

steps.title: Harden the Samples
steps.instruction: Harden the samples by placing them back in the dry ice chest.

substeps.instruction: Monitor the sample and remove it as soon as it turns completely white; do not overcool, as this can cause cracking and brittleness.

steps.title: Store and Log Samples
steps.instruction: Once the OCT has hardened, place the clamshell in the freezer.

substeps.instruction: Log the freezer location in the donor IT system.

steps.title: Clean Up
steps.instruction: Properly dispose of all biohazardous waste and other waste.
